model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary equity less CET1 retention, net debt zero

inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalent millions (1 ADS = 4 ordinary 25p shares), so per-share values are per ADS and match the NYSE quote. Start from 13,382.1M ordinary shares: the issued capital after cancelling buybacks executed through 25 Sep 2026, per the Total Voting Rights / buyback notices in the 1 Oct 2026 6-K batch. Add 435M dilutive share awards (H1-26 diluted weighted average 14,080M less basic 13,645M). Total 13,817M ordinary = 3,454.3M ADS. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flow and buybacks are value-neutral. About £0.4bn of the £1.0bn buyback announced 28 Jul 2026 is still to execute. The 14.0% pro-forma CET1 already deducts it, but the share count does not, so value per share is slightly understated if the remaining shares are bought below IV.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based payment charge, 652 (BCS_Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). Used as the TTM proxy: H1-26 interim does not split the charge out in the summary tables. SBC nets out of the bank flow either way, because 'ebitda' adds it back and sbc_pct removes it. It only moves the street basis.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases £2.24bn plus dividends £1.21bn. H1-26: £1.5bn of buybacks announced plus a £0.8bn interim dividend. The 2026-28 plan returns more than £15bn. Diluted share count fell from 17,668M (FY2020) to 14,080M (H1-26).
inputs.fx_note: Flows and balance sheet are in GBP millions. The quote is USD per ADS (1 ADS = 4 ordinary shares; shares_outstanding is already in ADS-equivalents). Model-to-quote rate is 1.324 USD per GBP (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-02T21:29Z). Parity check against the primary line: BARC.L closed at 443.65p (2026-10-02T15:37Z) x 4 / 100 x 1.324 = US$23.50 per ADS-equivalent, vs the NYSE ADS close of US$23.71. The 0.9% gap is close-time timing, which confirms the rate, its direction and the 4:1 ratio. GBP flows are discounted at a GBP cost of equity and converted at spot. refresh_price.py moves the ADS price but not this rate.
inputs.wacc_rationale: GBP cost of equity of 11.0%: 10-year gilt about 4.6%, plus beta about 1.25 x 5.0% ERP = 10.85%, rounded up. The beta is above the US bank precedents (WFC/USB 10.0% in USD) because about 48% of income is the Investment Bank, and GBP rates sit above USD. The rate is in the currency of the flows. One rate across all three scenarios: risk is carried in the bear path and its weight, not in a per-scenario premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable. The bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs, including occupancy, so no lease adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. AT1 coupons (£1,000M TTM) are tax-deductible in the UK, and their relief is booked in the tax charge, so they are removed GROSS pre-tax. NCI (£37M TTM) is grossed up at the ETR (£48M). 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - AT1 - NCI/(1-t), so the flow is profit attributable to ordinary equity holders. AT1 par (£12.7bn) is therefore NOT also deducted in the bridge (USB/WFC convention).
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine, with net_debt = 0. SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book. The house precedent for large banks (NAB.AX, USB, TFC, WFC, STT, NTRS) is FCFE-at-CoE on the engine route. That is the same economics (value = TNAV + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash, and it keeps BCS comparable to those names. Deposits (£594bn) are operating funding, not debt. OCF is meaningless for a bank (CSV OCF swings from -0.9bn to +60.7bn). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = Barclays 'total income' (NII + net fee, commission and other income), TTM Q3-25 to Q2-26 = 7,167 + 7,077 + 8,163 + 8,338 = 30,745 (H1-26 interim quarterly summary). This includes a c.£225M one-off Q2-26 gain on the AA card portfolio sale. 'ebitda' = PBT 10,002 + SBC 652 - AT1 1,000 - NCI 48 = 9,606 (31.2% margin), so the margin is PBT margin - 1.3pt (AT1+NCI 3.4% of revenue, SBC 2.1%). sbc_pct removes SBC. D&A is 0 (inside operating costs). Cash tax is the ETR on PBT less AT1: TTM 2,122 / 9,002 = 23.6%. 'capex' = CET1 retention that holds CET1/revenue at the pro-forma 51.1bn / 30.745bn = 1.662 as revenue grows: capex% = 166.2 x g/(1+g). FY0 check: (9,606 - 652) x (1 - 23.6%) = 6,841, vs reported TTM attributable profit of 6,843. CET1 is 14.0% pro-forma vs a 12.2% MDA requirement. The ~180bp cushion is the management buffer at the top of the 13-14% target range, so NO excess-capital credit goes in the bridge. Known RWA inflation of £19-26bn (Basel 3.1 from 1 Jan 2027, plus USCB IRB in H2-27) is deducted in equity_bridge, net of the guided Pillar 2A relief. Source: H1-2026 Half-Year Financial Report (6-K filed 2026-07-28, accession 0001654954-26-006931), not yet in Extracted/ (fetched from EDGAR).

equity_bridge.item: Basel 3.1 + USCB IRB RWA inflation, net of Pillar 2A relief
equity_bridge.note: H1-26 guidance: c.£19-26bn of RWAs from regulatory change (Basel 3.1 £8-15bn from 1 Jan 2027, plus USCB IRB c.£11bn in H2-27). Midpoint £22.5bn x 13.5% CET1 = c.£3.0bn of one-off retention. Less c.£1.0bn estimated benefit from the guided Pillar 2A reduction. The retention path grows CET1 only with revenue, so this step-up is not otherwise in the flows.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_3yr_cagr (total income FY2022-FY2025). It matches management's >5% 2025-28 income CAGR target.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (4.4% 3yr) diverges by more than 30% from the EPS CAGR (12.4%). About £8bn of buybacks over FY2021-25 cut the share count by about 17% while total equity grew slowly. Per-share growth (TNAVps +11.5% 3yr) is the better measure of value creation than total equity. The 5-year EPS and FCF CAGRs start at the FY2020 COVID-provision trough (EPS 8.6p) and are meaningless.
historical_growth.notes: 'FCF' here is the bank owner-flow proxy: profit attributable to ordinary equity holders (SBC is already a P&L expense). Reported FCF/OCF is not meaningful for a bank. Income growth was flat in FY2015-21 (restructuring and zero rates), then stepped up with the structural hedge and Tesco Bank (acquired Nov 2024).

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) ~ H2-26 implied by c.£31.5bn FY26 guidance (31.5 - 16.5 H1 = 15.0bn) + H1-27 on a >5% CAGR = ~£32.3bn, +5% on TTM. Fades to 2.5% GBP nominal by year 9.
base.margin_rationale: PBT margin 34.5% in year 1 (FY26 guidance: high-50s cost:income, LLR at the top of 50-60bps, so PBT ~£10.8bn on £31.5bn). 36.5% by the 2028 target year, with only partial delivery of the low-50s cost:income target (~54% vs 'low 50s'). Then a fade to 35.5% through the cycle. Implied RoTE ~13% in year 1 and ~14.5% in 2028, i.e. AT the >14% 2028 target and below the 16.1% Q2-26 print.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention = 1.662 x g/(1+g), which holds CET1 at 14.0% of RWA as RWA grows with income.
base.tax_rationale: ETR on PBT after AT1 coupons: FY25 23.7%, TTM 23.6%, H1-26 24.5%. Held at 24%. US DTA utilisation keeps cash tax below book tax (FY25 cash tax £1.39bn vs book £1.93bn); that is not credited.

bull.margin_rationale: Low-50s cost:income is delivered on schedule from >£2bn of gross efficiency savings, and the IB holds ~16% RoTE as markets stay strong. PBT margin ~39.5% from 2029, terminal RoTE ~16-17%, in line with the Q2-26 run-rate.

bear.margin_rationale: Markets revenue mean-reverts from a record H1-26, and a UK/US consumer credit cycle lifts LLR to ~100bps in year 2 (about £2bn above base). Motor-finance redress runs above the £430M provision once the Upper Tribunal rules. PBT margin falls to 25% in year 2, then recovers to 32% (cost:income stuck near 60%). Terminal RoTE ~11-12%, roughly the cost of equity. Year-2 retention is held at 0 rather than negative, because RWA procyclicality offsets the income decline.

scenario_narratives.base: Barclays hits its 2026 guidance (c.£31.5bn income, high-50s cost:income) and roughly its 2028 RoTE target (>14%). It does not sustain the 16% Q2-26 print. Income compounds at ~5% through 2028 on the locked-in structural hedge (>95% of 2026-28 hedge income secured), Tesco Bank and US card growth, then fades to UK nominal growth. Credit normalises at the top of the 50-60bps range. About two-thirds of earnings are distributed, consistent with the >£15bn 2026-28 return plan. CET1 is held at 14%, and the Basel 3.1/IRB RWA step-up is absorbed out of retained capital.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'all-weather' repositioning works. The Investment Bank keeps share in equities and financing, RWAs shift toward higher-returning UK and US consumer businesses, and the >£2bn efficiency program takes cost:income into the low 50s by 2028. Every segment stays ahead of target, as all did in Q2-26. RoTE settles at 16-17%, and the stock re-rates from about 1.1x TNAV toward peers on 1.5x+.
scenario_narratives.bear: Capital markets turn after a record 2025-26, while UK and US consumer credit deteriorate together, the exposure Tesco Bank and US cards growth added. The LLR doubles to ~100bps for a year, motor-finance redress runs well above the £430M provision, and income falls 3% in year 2. Cost:income stays near 60%. Barclays reverts to its historical pattern: RoTE around the cost of equity, and buybacks paused to rebuild CET1.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%. About 48% of income is the Investment Bank, so earnings are exposed to a markets downturn at a cyclical high. Consumer credit exposure has grown with Tesco Bank and US cards, and motor-finance redress is unresolved pending the Upper Tribunal. Bull is cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the IB to hold record-level returns while cost:income falls ~6pts. Base keeps 50%, anchored on twice-raised FY26 guidance and RoTE already above target. This is the same 25/50/25 as the WFC and TFC precedents.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth what it can pay ordinary shareholders after funding the capital its growth requires. The flow is profit attributable to ordinary equity holders (after AT1 coupons and NCI) less the CET1 retention that holds the ratio at 14%, discounted at a GBP cost of equity of 11%. Deposits are funding, not debt, so nothing is deducted for net debt. The value is therefore TNAV plus the PV of returns above the cost of equity. At a through-cycle RoTE of ~14-15%, Barclays earns a 3-4pt spread, which justifies roughly 1.3x TNAV. The ADS trades at about 1.06x TNAV (423p x 4 at the spot GBPUSD rate in fx_note). The GBP value converts to USD per ADS at spot, so a USD holder also carries GBP translation risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Investment Bank cyclicality: about 48% of H1-26 income. A markets downturn is the largest single swing factor, and it is the bear path.
Credit: base assumes LLR at the top of 50-60bps. A UK/US consumer cycle at ~100bps for a year costs about £2bn pre-tax.
Capital rules: Basel 3.1 (from Jan 2027) and the USCB IRB move add £19-26bn of RWAs. About £2bn net is deducted in the bridge, and the output floor reaches full weight in 2030.

Motor-finance redress: a £430M provision. Parts of the FCA scheme are suspended by the Upper Tribunal (hearing Dec-26/Feb-27), so the exposure is uncertain. It sits in the bear path; the engine's single bridge cannot hold a bear-only deduction.
UK bank tax/levy risk, and GBP/USD translation for ADS holders (the USD value per ADS moves one-for-one with GBPUSD).
Ring-fencing: Barclays is reportedly the only ring-fenced bank opposing reform, so it is a regulatory outlier.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 19.29-28.69 (USD per ADS). FX from Yahoo GBPUSD=X; BARC.L for the parity check.
data_sources.financials: BCS_Metrics.csv / core_metrics FY2015-FY2025 (20-F annuals). H1-2026 Half-Year Financial Report (SEC 6-K 2026-07-28, accession 0001654954-26-006931): quarterly income statement Q3-24 to Q2-26, CET1 £52.2bn / 14.3% (14.0% pro-forma), RWA £364.8bn, TNAVps 423p, diluted weighted average 14,080M, MDA requirement 12.2%, motor-finance provision £430M, 2026/2028 targets. Share count from the 1 Oct 2026 6-K batch (Total Voting Rights at 31 Aug 2026: 13,441.1M; after buyback cancellations to 25 Sep 2026: 13,382.1M).
data_sources.qualitative: BCS_Analysis.json (2026-10): FY26 income c.£31.5bn, NII ex-IB/HO >£13.7bn, high-50s cost:income, RoTE >12% (2026) / >14% (2028), >£15bn 2026-28 distributions, CET1 13-14%.
